name: Claude Code: permission rules and sandbox
covers: Claude Code only
price: Part of Claude Code, which needs a Claude subscription or an Anthropic Console account
limits: Its docs say deny rules match the command text Claude writes and are not a security boundary around a program; the OS-level sandbox is off by default and covers shell commands only.
summary: Deny, ask and allow rules evaluated deny first, plus an optional OS-level sandbox (Seatbelt on macOS, bubblewrap on Linux and WSL2) for shell commands.
content_note: the setting itself sends nothing; Claude Code sends your prompts and the files it reads to Anthropic, its model provider

name: Codex CLI: sandbox and approval modes
covers: Codex only
price: Free CLI; used with a ChatGPT plan or an API key
limits: A setting of the agent itself: the danger-full-access mode and the never-ask approval policy are one configuration change away.
summary: Sandbox modes read-only, workspace-write and danger-full-access, and approval modes on-request and never, with finer-grained approval settings in its config. On Linux the sandbox uses bubblewrap and seccomp.
content_note: the setting itself sends nothing; Codex sends your prompts and the files it reads to OpenAI, its model provider

name: Gitleaks
covers: Any agent or person, at commit or scan time
price: Free
limits: Pattern-based detection of secrets already written to files or commits; as a pre-commit hook it can stop a commit, not an agent reading a secret.
summary: Finds passwords, API keys and tokens in git repos, files and piped input. Runs as a CLI, a pre-commit hook or in CI.

name: Microsoft Presidio
covers: Any pipeline you place it in, before text reaches an agent or model
price: Free
limits: Its own docs warn there is no guarantee it finds all sensitive information, so it reduces what reaches the agent rather than guaranteeing it.
summary: Identifies and anonymizes personal data in text, as a Python library, a Docker service or on Kubernetes.

name: HashiCorp Vault
covers: Any agent or program that asks it for a secret
price: Free to run under its licence; an Enterprise edition is sold
limits: It gates the secrets it holds, not a secret already copied into a file the agent can read, and its audit log is a record you keep, not a proof an outsider can check.
summary: Stores secrets encrypted, issues short-lived dynamic credentials, and applies access control with a detailed audit log, outside the agent.

name: NoData
open_source: Apache-2.0 for the verification layer; the service is closed
covers: Agents connected through its MCP gate
price: Early access; pricing is not published yet
limits: Controls only what passes through it; access an agent already holds in the clear is outside it.
summary: Seals files and secrets on your computer to keys you hold, decides each release before it happens, and signs receipts that its published verifiers check offline.
disclosure: Made by the team behind this site.
content_note: only ciphertext and hashes leave your computer

name: AGENTS.md and other instruction files
covers: Any agent that reads the file: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, Cursor rules, Copilot instructions
price: Free
limits: Text the model reads as context. The agent can ignore it, and anyone who can write to the repository can change it. Rule files have also been used as an attack channel.
summary: A file in the repository that tells the agent how to work and what not to touch. AGENTS.md is an open format now held by the Agentic AI Foundation.

name: Gemini CLI: sandbox, trusted folders and confirmations
content_note: the agent sends prompts and context to its model provider
covers: Gemini CLI only
price: Free CLI; used with a Google account, a Gemini API key or Vertex AI
limits: Its configuration docs say sandboxing is disabled by default, and the default macOS profile leaves the network open. Trusted folders are off by default.
summary: Confirmation prompts for tool calls, trusted folders, and an optional sandbox: Seatbelt profiles on macOS or a Docker or Podman container.

name: TruffleHog
content_note: to verify a finding it sends the found credential to the service it belongs to
open_source: AGPL-3.0; an Enterprise edition is sold
covers: Any agent or person, at scan or commit time
price: Free; Enterprise priced separately
limits: Finds and reports secrets already written somewhere. As a local hook, a commit made with --no-verify skips it, and it does not stop an agent from reading a secret.
summary: Finds credentials in git history, files, buckets and other sources, and checks which of them are still live.

name: GitHub secret scanning and push protection
content_note: the code is already on GitHub; the scan runs there
covers: Any agent or person pushing to a GitHub repository
price: Free for public repositories; paid for private ones (GitHub Secret Protection)
limits: Its docs say that by default anyone with write access can bypass push protection by giving a reason, so an agent holding a writer's token can too. Delegated bypass, where someone else approves, is opt-in.
summary: Blocks a push that contains a recognised secret, on GitHub's servers, before it lands, and alerts on secrets already in the repository.

name: GitGuardian ggshield AI hooks
content_note: scanned content goes to the GitGuardian API unless you run it self-hosted
open_source: MIT for the ggshield CLI; the platform is proprietary
covers: AI coding tools whose hook systems it is installed into, such as Claude Code, Cursor and Codex
price: Free tier; paid plans for teams
limits: Its docs say that when misconfigured it fails open, and the interaction proceeds with a warning. The hook runs in the agent's own hook configuration on the developer's machine.
summary: Scans prompts, files and tool calls for secrets through the coding agent's hooks, and can block the interaction before the secret reaches the model.

name: LLM Guard: Anonymize and Deanonymize
covers: Any application that calls it before and after the model
price: Free
limits: A library the application chooses to call, so a code path that skips it is not covered. It masks only what it detects, and the originals sit in a vault object inside the same process.
summary: Replaces personal data in prompts with placeholders and restores the originals in the model's answer. Maintained by Protect AI, now part of Palo Alto Networks.

name: Google Cloud Sensitive Data Protection
covers: Any pipeline that calls its API before text reaches an agent or model
price: Usage-based, per amount of data inspected or transformed
limits: The application decides whether to call it, and it transforms only the infoTypes it detects. Reversing a token needs the KMS-wrapped key, gated by IAM.
summary: Detects sensitive data and masks it, or replaces it with reversible tokens (deterministic encryption or format-preserving encryption) under a key wrapped by your Cloud KMS key.

name: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails: sensitive information filters
covers: Prompts and responses of models called through Amazon Bedrock, or any text sent to ApplyGuardrail
price: Usage-based, per text unit
limits: AWS docs say the filter does not evaluate tool-call arguments, tool results or tool definitions, so personal data there is neither blocked nor masked. AWS calls the filter probabilistic.
summary: Blocks or masks personal data in prompts and responses on the Bedrock API, with custom patterns. An IAM condition can force a guardrail on every model call.

name: Docker MCP Gateway
open_source: MIT (the gateway); the enterprise policy features are commercial
covers: MCP servers an agent reaches through the gateway
price: Free gateway; enterprise pricing not published
limits: An agent with another MCP configuration, or direct file or network access, does not pass through it. Secret blocking is pattern-based. The gateway has had published advisories of its own.
summary: Runs MCP servers in containers behind one gateway outside the agent, injects their secrets at call time, and can block secrets in payloads. An enterprise tier adds Cedar policies with required approval.

name: agentgateway
covers: MCP, agent-to-agent and model traffic routed through it
price: Free
limits: Only as strong as the network isolation of the servers behind it: a direct path to a backend skips it. The rules are written by the operator.
summary: A gateway hosted by the Agentic AI Foundation that authorises each MCP tool call with CEL rules that can read the tool name and its arguments.

name: Pomerium: MCP support
open_source: Apache-2.0 source; official builds use the Pomerium Community License; an Enterprise edition is sold
covers: MCP servers placed behind it
price: Free core; Enterprise pricing not published
limits: Its changelog labels MCP support experimental. A client that reaches the MCP server without going through Pomerium is not covered.
summary: An identity-aware proxy that puts MCP servers behind single sign-on and applies policy per tool before the call reaches the server.

name: Kong AI Gateway: AI MCP Proxy
content_note: only when you run it on Kong Konnect
open_source: Kong Gateway core is Apache-2.0; the MCP OAuth2 plugin is Enterprise
covers: MCP servers proxied through Kong
price: Enterprise; pricing not published
limits: Direct calls to the upstream MCP server skip it. Its docs call the MCP OAuth2 plugin a Tech Preview available only in the Enterprise offering.
summary: Proxies MCP servers with default and per-tool access lists per consumer group, and can map OAuth token claims to consumers.

name: Infisical Agent Vault
content_note: only when you use Infisical Cloud
open_source: Open source (Agent Vault); Infisical core MIT with enterprise parts
covers: API calls a coding agent makes through the proxy
price: Not published for Agent Vault (preview)
limits: In preview. Calls that skip the proxy are not covered, and Infisical's separate MCP server hands secret values to the agent, so the product matters, not the brand.
summary: A credential proxy that adds API keys to an agent's requests at the network edge, so the agent makes the call without ever seeing the key.

name: Aembit MCP Identity Gateway
covers: Agents and workloads that reach services through Aembit Edge or the gateway
price: Not published
limits: A static credential the agent already holds, or a path not routed through Aembit, is outside it. Its docs say the gateway pattern adds latency and a single point of failure.
summary: Gives each agent an attested identity and exchanges it, per request, for the downstream credential, so the agent never holds the secret.

name: 1Password Secure Agentic Autofill
covers: Browser agents running on Browserbase
price: Early access for 1Password Enterprise customers
limits: Early access, and only on Browserbase. After login the agent acts with that session.
summary: A browser agent asks to log in, a person approves on their own 1Password app, and 1Password fills the password in without the model ever seeing it.

name: Cloudflare AI Gateway
covers: Model calls an application sends through the gateway
price: Core features free; AI detections in the WAF are a paid Enterprise add-on
limits: Its docs say DLP does not inspect base64 or binary content and is skipped on cache hits. A caller holding its own provider key can go around the gateway; keeping that key only in the gateway narrows this.
summary: An edge gateway in front of model providers that can block prompts or responses on guardrails and DLP profiles, and can hold the provider keys so the application does not.

name: NVIDIA NeMo Guardrails
covers: Model and tool calls wired through its rails
price: Free; NVIDIA NIM microservices sold separately
limits: It enforces only where it is wired in. Run as a library inside the application, it is the application's own code, close to level 2; it sits outside the agent only as a separate server.
summary: A framework for input, output, retrieval and execution rails around a model or agent, run as a library or as a separate guardrails server.

name: Lasso MCP Gateway
open_source: MIT (the MCP gateway); the Lasso platform is commercial
covers: MCP servers an agent reaches through the gateway
price: Free gateway; platform pricing not published
limits: Traffic that does not pass through the gateway is not seen. It inspects and masks what passes; it does not encrypt the data behind it.
summary: An open-source gateway between the agent and its MCP servers that scans and masks requests and responses and can block risky servers.

name: OpenTDF
covers: Data wrapped in the Trusted Data Format, read by any client that asks its key access server
price: Free
limits: Once an entitled reader gets the key, the plaintext is theirs. Its docs do not say whether authorisation decisions are cached. Policy applies to the whole object, not to parts of it.
summary: Data stays encrypted; the key access server rewraps the key only after the authorisation service confirms the person or agent may open it. Virtru's products are built on it.

name: Google Workspace client-side encryption
content_note: Google stores only ciphertext; the key service is yours or a partner's
open_source: proprietary (the key service API is public)
covers: Docs, Sheets, Slides, Drive files, Gmail and Meet for users of qualifying editions
price: Included in Enterprise Plus, Education and Frontline Plus editions; key service partners priced separately
limits: Google services lose search and preview over encrypted content, and mobile is view-only. Anyone authorised by your identity provider and the file's sharing gets plaintext on their device.
summary: Content is encrypted in the browser; on every open, your key service checks an authentication and an authorisation token before it unwraps the key. Google never holds it.

name: Microsoft Purview Double Key Encryption
content_note: Microsoft cannot open the content without your key
open_source: proprietary (Microsoft publishes a reference key service)
covers: Office files and email labelled with a DKE label, on Windows desktop apps
price: Needs Microsoft 365 E5-class licensing
limits: Microsoft says Copilot and agents cannot access this data, and it also loses web apps, co-authoring, search, eDiscovery and DLP in SharePoint and OneDrive.
summary: Two keys: Microsoft holds one, your own key service holds the other and releases it for each authorised Entra ID user, so Microsoft alone cannot open the file.

name: Virtru Data Harbor Platform
content_note: content stays encrypted; keys are Virtru-hosted unless you choose your own key store
open_source: Built on OpenTDF (open source); the platform is commercial
covers: Data wrapped in TDF and the agents and applications that request it through its SDK, CLI, MCP or proxies
price: Not published
limits: Launched on 2026-11-17; the key-release mechanics here come from OpenTDF's docs. Keys are Virtru-hosted by default. An entitled agent receives plaintext, and the signed decision records are so far a launch claim.
summary: Wraps data so that an agent receives a file's key only after an authorisation decision on that agent, aimed at AI agents and their tools.
